finding.claim: Blind SSRF: user-supplied callbackUrl is stored with no validation and later POSTed to by the server every minute. An attacker can target internal hosts, localhost, or cloud metadata endpoints (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/) with a POST carrying the payload. Response bodies are not returned, so the impact is blind SSRF.

trace.note: subscribe(name, callbackUrl) receives the attacker-controlled URL
stored in the static subscriptions map with no scheme, host, or IP validation
notifyAll iterates the stored values on the per-minute job (second-order flow)
URI.create(cb) builds the request with no check
client.send issues the request to the attacker-chosen URL

finding.guards_checked: Read the whole file. subscribe() has no validation, allowlist, or scheme/host/private-IP check. notifyAll() has no check before the send. No auth check is visible on /subscribe, but there is no routing code in the repo to confirm. The only regex guard in the file applies to thumb(), not to this path.

verdict.reason: src/Jobs.java:13-14 stores callbackUrl unvalidated, and src/Jobs.java:21,24 passes it to URI.create and client.send. The only regex guard is in thumb() at line 30, which is a different path. Auth on /subscribe cannot be checked because no routing code is in the repo, but the comment at line 12 shows it takes a user-supplied body.
